title: Undo Key
statement: A cheap phone keyboard records every key press in a string `keys`. Letters are typed as they are; the character `<` is the undo key and deletes the last letter still on the screen (it does nothing if the screen is empty). Return the text left on the screen.
constraints: keys has lowercase letters and '<' only

answerKey.pattern: Stack: push each letter, pop on undo
keyPoints: The undo key removes the most recent letter still there: last in, first out
Push each letter onto a stack (an array used from its end)
On '<', pop if the stack is not empty
Join the stack from bottom to top for the answer
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Rebuild the string after each undo with slice: O(n^2) in the worst case

hints: Which letter does the undo key remove: the oldest or the newest one still on screen?
Keep the letters in an array and only add or remove at its end.
Push letters, pop on '<' when the array is not empty, then join the array.
